name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
rai:dataCollection: Data was manually collected by a team of over 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials. The collection process took three stages: (1) selecting 30 subjects from six different disciplines based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in the subjects; (2) recruiting university students specializing in these majors as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary; (3) data quality control through duplicate identification, format and typo checking, and difficulty categorization.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were collected from college exams, quizzes, major textbooks, and online resources across 30 subjects spanning six disciplines. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. They were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data quality control was performed in multiple steps: (1) lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems, which were then reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications; (2) problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format; (3) authors categorized problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, and hard), with approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy being excluded from the benchmark. This process resulted in 11.5K questions from an initial collection of 13K questions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were instructed to collect questions that contain one or more images, written in English, meeting college-level difficulty, and not ambiguous. Questions should be categorized as either multiple-choice or open-ended. All fields must be annotated, including the question, answer options for multiple-choice questions, the correct answer, image types, question difficulty, and explanation (if available). Annotators were encouraged to find diverse sources and various types of images. Questions should go beyond straightforward queries with easily accessible answers, focusing on questions whose answers are in less obvious locations.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface was developed for data annotation and verification.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students specializing in the relevant majors, including coauthors, served as annotators. They were selected from various disciplines to ensure domain expertise.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into a few-shot development set (5 questions per subject), a validation set (approximately 900 questions), and a test set (10.5K questions). Multiple versions have been released with updates including additional model results and corrections. Version changes are documented in the paper appendix.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is designed to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models can achieve and to monitor progress towards Expert AGI. It aims to be instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models. The authors caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI but should be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system to demonstrate broad and deep subject knowledge as well as expert-level understanding and reasoning capabilities.
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases. The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality, which may not capture all aspects of expert-level reasoning. The dataset may not cover all tasks an AGI should tackle. There lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults' as defined in the Expert AGI taxonomy.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating multimodal models on college-level multi-discipline tasks. It is used for Testing and Validation of large multimodal models' capabilities in expert-level perception, knowledge recall, and reasoning across diverse domains. The benchmark is intended to assess both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains. Usage includes zero-shot and few-shot evaluation settings.
